title: Rav Chiyya bar Assi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Eruvin 59b; Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Ashi. Likewise in Taanit 18a, “Rav Chiyya bar Assi said that Rav said” — Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Ashi. In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 3:8, Rabbi Chiyya bar Assi in the name of Asa; Hyman suggests that perhaps there too it should read bar Ashi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 8:9.

And what is cited in Midrash Tehillim 72:6, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Assi said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: The Land of Israel will in the future produce cakes,” Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef, as in Ketubot 111b.
In Gittin 22a, “Rabbi Chiyya bar Assi in Ulla’s name,” Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Chiyya bar Ami.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Ketubot 111b has Chiyya bar Yosef; saved Gittin 22a retains Chiyya bar Assi. Hyman’s Ashi/Yosef/Ami corrections are attributed and not automatically imposed on the named witnesses. The Gittin 8:9 locator is Jerusalem Talmud.

The inspected Gittin 22a still reads Chiyya bar Assi in Ulla’s name, while Ketubot 111b reads Chiyya bar Yosef. The exact Dikdukei Soferim Ashi readings and Hyman’s proposed Ami correction have not been independently established from those editions.
